rationale:
REVISED 20 Sep after his amend. Two things in it.

(1) He cannot run Sunday 27th. The long run moves to Saturday 26th and Sunday becomes rest, with Tue-Fri stepped up a kilometre each to keep the week's progression intact: 5, 6, 7, 8, then 14 on Saturday. That is ~40km against the ~46km originally proposed. The shortfall is deliberate rather than reluctant — it is a recovery week after a maximal half, and less is the safer error.

(2) He pushed back on the review's reading of the opening 5km, and he is right. The review called it 'a hard opening 5km that the finish and decoupling forgave rather than validated'. His account — going slightly quicker but holding back, a net downhill opening, and tucking in out of a slight headwind — is better supported by the data than the review's hedge was. His HR over km 1-6 ran 152, 159, 163, 161, 165, 163 against a race average of 164: he was settling INTO race effort by km 3, not exceeding it. Alice's elevation deltas put km 1-5 at 14m net downhill. And the two facts that settle it are that his last kilometre (3:38.3) was the fastest of the race and the second 10km was only 24 seconds slower than the first — neither happens off an opening that was genuinely too hard. The review under-weighted the drafting and the gradient. Validated, not forgiven.

Everything else stands: easy only, no quality, no strides, the first Saturday since May without a session, and the Saturday/Wednesday structure resuming on evidence rather than a date. The Guy Fawkes sharpening block still gets shaped next Sunday, once this week's recovery is visible.

ASSUMPTION worth confirming: that Sunday alone is unavailable. If he is away for several days, this needs rewriting again, not nudging.

changes.notes: Rest - the normal Monday, and doubly right after yesterday's effort.

RECOVERY WEEK BEGINS. Easy, short, entirely by feel - roughly 20-30 min, walk if anything feels off. No strides, no pace target. Yesterday was RPE 8 with a full sprint to the line; the legs get nothing asked of them today regardless of how good they feel.
Easy 30-35 min, still entirely by feel, no pace target, no strides. If yesterday felt heavy rather than just tired, take today as a second rest day instead - better to lose a day here than force it.
Easy 7km - building duration gently, still conversational throughout. First day back on anything like a normal easy run.

First long run back, MOVED from Sunday because he cannot run the 27th. 14km genuinely easy throughout, no pace target. Aerobic volume, not a rehearsal for anything. Still the first Saturday since May without a quality session - deliberate, not a gap to fill.
Rest - he cannot run today, and after a recovery week ending in the long run on Saturday that is the right shape anyway.
